generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, learning by doing takes several forms. Placements put you into clinical, educational and occupational settings. Fieldwork takes you out to observe behaviour in a community. Laboratory studies let you run real experiments, and live projects, such as designing a survey for a real client, give you real work with real consequences. Each is a different shape of the same idea: you learn psychology by practising it.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students are each offered a piece of learning by doing.

Tom is told his activity is 'just a lab study' and assumes it does not really count, because it is not a proper clinical placement. He almost dismisses it, thinking practice- and work-based learning only means one thing.

Amara recognises her own survey project for a real community group as the same kind of learning, in a different form. It is not a placement, but it is real work with real consequences, so it is learning by doing, shaped to fit psychology.

Both were offered practice- and work-based learning. Only Amara saw that it comes in many forms, and that a lab study and a live project both count.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, practice- and work-based learning takes many forms: clinical, educational and occupational placements, fieldwork, laboratory studies and live projects. You can now recognise that range and give an example in psychology. What they share is learning by doing. The next lesson turns to why this kind of learning is so valuable to you.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara understand that Tom did not?

items.text: That a live survey project is learning by doing, just in a different form from a placement.
That a lab study is the only real form of learning by doing.
That practice- and work-based learning only counts in a clinic.
That her project did not really count as learning.

feedback.correct: That's right. A live project is practice- and work-based learning in a different form from a placement.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara recognised about the different forms this learning can take.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara understood that her live survey project is practice- and work-based learning in a different form from a clinical placement.
